answer: A sponsor carries 58% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the haven liability is recorded in the pulse ledger at admission, the tide audit exposes the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must as a result place its own capital behind each extra identity it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 21 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
